t: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the acceptable market name of any engineered animal approved prior to the effective date of the National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard (February 19, 2019) shall include the words “genetically engineered” prior to the existing acceptable market name.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the reference to the National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard, itself a product of rulemaking, implies a regulatory process with public comment. That fails because this section is a direct statutory labeling mandate set by Congress. It does not authorize or require rulemaking, a hearing, an advisory body, consultation with any outside party, or a right to sue, so no one outside the federal government is brought into a federal decision.
fable.s: the acceptable market name of any engineered animal approved prior to the effective date of the National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard (February 19, 2019) shall include the words “genetically engineered” prior to the existing acceptable market name.

opus.w: This section sets a labeling rule directly: market names for certain engineered animals must include "genetically engineered." No one outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any federal decision. The mention of the Disclosure Standard only marks a date. It does not require or authorize rulemaking, so it is not participation.
opus.s: the acceptable market name of any engineered animal approved prior to the effective date of the National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard (February 19, 2019) shall include the words “genetically engineered” prior to the existing acceptable market name.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** The tempting reading is that the reference to the "National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard," a federal rule made through rulemaking, brings in participation. It doesn't. The section only names that standard to set a cutoff date. It does not require or authorize any new rulemaking, comment period, hearing, consultation or advisory body. It simply sets a naming rule directly by statute.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates a specific labeling requirement for engineered animals. It does not involve the federal government consulting or coordinating with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The definition of participation requires interaction where outsiders influence a federal decision, whereas this is a substantive rule imposed on manufacturers. There is no advisory board, comment period, or consultation mechanism described here.
qwen_chat.s: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the acceptable market name of any engineered animal approved prior to the effective date of the National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard (February 19, 2019) shall include the words “genetically engineered” prior to the existing acceptable market name.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement to use the term "genetically engineered" constitutes a form of public participation because it informs the public. However, this is a labeling requirement imposed on manufacturers, not a process where the public or outside entities consult with or coordinate with the government to influence a decision. The definition of participation requires the government to consult or coordinate with people outside the government *before* making a decision. This section mandates a specific label for products already approved; it does not describe a process of consultation, comment, or advisory input from outsiders into the regulatory decision-making process itself.
